name: How much contingency should I budget for a luxury custom home?

mainEntity.name: What contingency budget should I set for a luxury custom home in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What contingency budget should I set for a luxury custom home in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contingency is one of the most important parts of a luxury custom home budget because even careful planning cannot eliminate every unknown. In Los Angeles, common budget surprises include soil conditions, utility upgrades, inspection-driven changes, custom fabrication delays, and owner-requested upgrades after construction begins. The amount needed depends on project complexity, but the key is to keep contingency separate from the base construction budget so it is available when genuinely needed. Homeowners should also distinguish between contingency for unforeseen conditions and allowance overages for upgrades they may choose later. A builder should explain how contingency is tracked, who can authorize its use, and what happens if it is not fully spent. A clear contingency strategy protects the schedule and reduces stress when changes arise during the build.
acceptedAnswer.description: A luxury custom home budget should include a contingency because site conditions, design changes, and material price shifts are common. Many projects need more than a small reserve, especially if the lot is steep, the scope is highly customized, or the permit process is still evolving.
